adorn

/uh-DORN/ — rhymes with corn · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To adorn something is to decorate it in order to make it more attractive.

Villagers adorned the square with lanterns for the festival.

Example

To adorn the school gym for the winter dance, students string lights from beam to beam, hang garlands along the walls, and place flower arrangements on every table.

Adorn captures not just 'to decorate' but 'to decorate specifically in order to make something more beautiful'—that purposeful enhancement of beauty is what makes adorn more precise than the plain word 'decorate.'

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

decorate: Decorate is the plain, everyday word for adding attractive things to a space or object — you can decorate quickly, casually, or just for fun. Adorn is more deliberate: to adorn something is to decorate it carefully, with the specific purpose of making it more beautiful.

embellish: To embellish is to add extra ornamental touches to something already finished — a flourish here, a detail there, laid on top of a completed design. To adorn is broader: it names the whole act of decorating a thing to make it more beautiful, not just the extras added at the end.

garnish: Garnish is the kitchen's word: to garnish is to decorate food with small finishing touches, like a sprig of herbs on a plate. Adorn reaches far wider — you can adorn a robe, a room, or a whole square — and it always means decorating to make the thing more beautiful.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

strip: to remove decorations or coverings from something

deface: to spoil or ruin something's appearance

Where it sits · how dressed up something is

bare → decorated → ornate → adorn

bare vs. adorn: Bare is the starting point far below adorned: a bare wall has nothing on it at all, while an adorned wall has been decorated to please the eye.

decorated vs. adorn: Decorated and adorned are close in strength, but adorn carries extra care: to adorn something is to decorate it deliberately in order to make it more beautiful.

ornate vs. adorn: Ornate is a step beyond adorned: an adorned room has attractive touches added to it, while an ornate room is covered in elaborate detail everywhere you look.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ad-: to, toward (Latin)

Root — orn: to decorate, equip, furnish (Latin)

Put it together: Ad- means 'to' and orn- means 'to decorate or equip,' so adorn literally means 'to add decoration to' — exactly what you do when you adorn something to make it more attractive.

Use the root in a new word: ornament: Every December, Maya hangs her favorite ornament on the highest branch of the tree.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Use adorn for formal, intentional decoration meant to enhance beauty or for aesthetic effect. The simpler 'decorate' works fine for everyday contexts.
